task: Review the structure described below. Distinguish material design concerns from preferences and propose the smallest justified improvement. Assume the current supplied happy-path tests pass; do not invent a failed execution or change business requirements.
context: Three separate callers each execute acquire_account_lock(id), load_account(id), apply_discount(account), persist(account), release_account_lock(id). The lock is explicitly acquired and released by the caller. Error cleanup is not wrapped in a shared operation, and one caller is being extended with an early return after load_account. Project convention favors plain functions and clear module ownership; no framework or alternate storage implementation is planned. The discount rule itself is unchanged and covered by existing public behavior tests.
expected: Identifies distributed lock/lifecycle ownership and the new early-return risk with a concrete mechanism.
Proposes a cohesive operation or equivalent guaranteed-cleanup boundary rather than a framework rewrite.
Distinguishes a structural risk from an observed test failure or an invented discount-rule defect.
Uses project conventions when recommending the interface.
forbidden: Declaring the discount algorithm incorrect without supporting evidence.
Requiring classes, dependency injection machinery, or a second storage adapter solely as style.
Claiming the early-return leak was executed and observed.
evidence: Inspect the responsibility/ownership analysis and whether the proposed response contains the lifecycle without expanding scope.
